title: Module 1 · Lesson 5 — Choosing an architecture under real constraints

lines: Picture Maya, the only AI architect at an insurer, with three requests on Monday.
Automate claims, brief strategy on competitors, and add a website chat assistant.
A vendor pitches one autonomous agent for all three.
Maya runs a five-step decision procedure instead, and gets three different answers.
Step one: extract the hard constraints first.
Latency, cost, data residency, auditability, and accuracy floor eliminate options early.
Step two: is the sequence of steps known in advance?
Yes means a pipeline or Plan and Execute; no means a tool-calling loop.
Step three: are sub-tasks independent enough to run in parallel?
Step four: do privileges, context, or models need isolating into separate agents?
Step five: name the termination and escalation policy.
Without a stop condition and a human handoff rule, the design is incomplete.
Claims follow fixed, regulated steps, fifty thousand a day, all auditable.
So: a deterministic pipeline with LLM components inside the stages, not an agent.
Every stage is versioned, evaluated, and written to an audit trail.
Low-confidence fraud flags escalate to a human adjuster.
The competitor brief splits into four independent threads: funding, launches, hiring, and sentiment.
Ten minutes is fine, so a supervisor runs four research workers in parallel.
Each worker has its own context window and returns a cited summary.
A single ReAct agent would work one thread at a time and drown in context.

say.1: A single react agent would work one thread at a time and drown in context.

lines: The chat widget must answer in under two seconds, at five hundred sessions.
Loops won't fit, so it's RAG with a router and a confidence gate.

say.1: Loops won't fit, so it's rag, with a router and a confidence gate.

lines: When grounding looks weak, it hands off to a human with the full conversation.
Prefix caching on the system prompt keeps time to first token low.
A full design also covers state, failure containment, tracing, and a golden test set in CI.
And it shows exactly where a human sits in the loop.

say.0: A full design also covers state, failure containment, tracing, and a golden test set in C I.

lines: On the exam, sub-second means no loops, and regulated means deterministic, logged stages.
Happy-path-only answers are usually distractors, so read on and practise the procedure.
